content.title: Guardians vs. Dodgers: Prediction, Lineups, How to Watch (3/31)
content.text: The Cleveland Guardians (3–2) and the Los Angeles Dodgers (3–1) continue their three-game series tonight at Dodger Stadium. The Guardians opened this series with a statement 4–2 win on Monday, handing the Dodgers their first loss of the season. Cleveland leaned on a dominant outing from Parker Messick, who threw six scoreless innings while allowing just five hits and striking out five. Cleveland got on board first off a Steven Kwan RBI double in the top of the third. They added three more in the seventh, with Rhys Hoskins walking with the bases loaded to force a run, followed by a two-run double off the bat of Daniel Schneemann to extend the lead to 4–0. The Dodgers mounted a late push in the ninth with an RBI double from Mookie Betts and a groundout from Freddie Freeman that brought in Betts. But the rally fizzled out. Roki Sasaki had a short but effective outing for the Dodgers after an awful spring. He pitched just four innings, allowing one run and four hits, while striking out four. Shohei Ohtani makes his first start of the season tonight. He allowed three runs over 8.1 innings in two outings this spring, striking out 15. Tanner Bibee takes the mound for the Guardians, making his second start of the season after giving up three runs and four hits — including three homers — on Opening Day against the Seattle Mariners. Expect the Dodger bats to bounce back against Bibee as Ohtani keeps the Guardians in check.
